The payoff came in reuse: after twenty cycles, the plain support kept 86 percent of its activity and the coated one 73 percent, while free enzyme died after a single use. Cold storage for sixty days told the same story, with the coated support holding 60 percent against the free enzyme's 17. The authors present the magnetically recoverable enzyme as a reusable capture catalyst.
pmc-13563959:
RuoFeng Wang leads a 2026 review of USP14, a protein that removes ubiquitin tags and sits on the cell's protein-recycling machinery, and of its widening role in cancer. Once seen mainly as a helper that stabilizes cancer-promoting proteins, it now links to the tumor surroundings and to treatment resistance. It also has jobs that do not involve its cutting action at all.

Readers working on new cancer drugs get a systems view of one regulator and the openings it may offer for treatment.
pmc-13570859:
Masahiko Nakatsui and colleagues test, in a 2026 historical cohort study, whether free-text Japanese medical records gathered under a national data law can rebuild survival results from a major lung cancer trial. Seventy-five patients treated with the immune drug atezolizumab were identified, trial eligibility rules were applied, and trained reviewers extracted outcomes by hand from unstructured notes.

Median time before the cancer worsened came to three and a half months, close to the figure in the trial's Japanese subgroup. Patterns by disease stage and fitness matched clinical expectation. Median overall survival could not yet be calculated. The close match supports using such real-world records to check trial findings in everyday practice.
pmc-13571359:
Katharina M. Wörgötter and colleagues present, in a 2026 report of three cases, a mapping-guided way to biopsy heart muscle when cardiac sarcoidosis is suspected. This inflammatory disease scars the heart, yet standard blind biopsy often misses it. Electrical maps of the heart locate abnormal low-voltage tissue so samples can be taken where disease actually lives.

European guidelines in 2025 gave the method a formal recommendation for the first time. The cases show both the gains and the limits of the approach inside a wider diagnostic workup.
pmc-13572359:
Chaopeng Mei and a large team study, in a 2026 set of mouse and cell experiments, a brake enzyme called DUSP10 in severe acute pancreatitis. This pancreatic emergency can fail several organs through body-wide inflammation. The enzyme fell in disease models, so the team removed it genetically, added it back with a virus carrier, and traced its binding partners.

The enzyme binds and switches off a signaling protein called TAK1, and blocking either that protein or the fiery death route rescued deficient animals. Restoring this brake looks like a plausible treatment direction for a disease with few options.
pmc-13572459:
B. Santhosh Reddy, with five colleagues, presents a 2026 design for neural networks that can repair themselves after damage. Networks in safety-linked systems can suffer broken inner parts or attacks that feed them crafted inputs. Full retraining is slow and costly, so the design aims for small, local fixes instead.

The model scans each layer for odd activity, finds the faulty layer, and retrains only a light patch for that spot. Tests ran on four image data sets, from hand digits to street-style photos. After parts were zeroed out, accuracy bounced back near the intact level, at 97.33 and 97.22 percent against a 97.76 percent base in one case. The repair adds little compute or memory load. The authors pitch it for systems that must keep running without a full rebuild.
pmc-13572559:

The flow, called MHD bioconvective nanofluid flow, responds to a magnetic field, heat rays, and the fluid's own changing thickness. Such flows show up in micro devices, nutrient transport in water, and biofuel cells.

Outputs cover microbe density, heat, and concentration profiles, shown in graphs. The ranked list tells designers which knobs matter most for each output.
pmc-13573059:

The review sorts cases by how firm the glue claim is, from proven seams to pairs that await sharp structural proof. Cases span signal proteins, gene control parts, and membrane receptors. The authors argue the glue role has been under-rated and call for a systematic structural hunt. Such a hunt could seed new drugs that work by sticking proteins together on purpose.
pmc-13573459:

A glue system then fixed the binding tips of both SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV onto the cages. In mice, the paired vaccine raised stronger antibody and T cell responses than single versions. Two doses guarded engineered mice against live challenge with both viruses. No body-wide harm appeared.
pmc-13574759:

Calcium silicate cements set by taking up water, and blood often seeps into the work zone during root procedures. A push-out test gauged bond strength, and nuclear magnetic scans read the silicate chain growth inside. Blood cut bond strength for the classic product but raised it for one rival, with no clear change for two others. pmc-13574859:

pmc-13575059:

Scores varied widely between patients, yet adding avelumab did not shift them in a meaningful way. Survival and time without progression were similar across risk groups. The authors present the work as exploratory, noting that measured interaction burden showed no link to outcomes here.
pmc-13575159:

A graphical interface lets clinicians enter patient details and line settings, then watch the fluid behaviour in real time. Users can test setups before use and compare options side by side. The authors present the tool as a teaching and planning aid for safer neonatal care.
pmc-13576259:

pmc-13576359:

pmc-13577559:

pmc-13578259:

After such surgery a strap or bandage presses on the chest to limit fluid buildup. The team enrolled adults at one center in China and assigned them to the new strap or to standard bandages.

pmc-13578759:

The authors cast brusatol as a promising partner drug, with animal and safety work still ahead before any patient use.
pmc-13579959:

pmc-13584359:

The authors urge better clinical access, language help, and career guidance.
pmc-13585559:

pmc-13586159:

They caught change over time and key shifts from normal thinking to mild trouble and from mild trouble to Alzheimer's. pmc-13587559:

Their 2026 study covered 45 middle schools in Guangzhou with close to four thousand students. Bacterial mixes differed clearly between the two room types, with some environmental genera richer where rhinitis was rare and gut-type genera richer where it was common. Close to four hundred compounds also split the rooms. One bacterium's link with rhinitis even flipped direction depending on the level of a certain fatty compound beside it. pmc-13588459:

pmc-13590159:

pmc-13590559:

Stiffness and shaking grew more common as prolactin rose, yet one low prolactin drug still carried high shaking risk. pmc-13591259:

pmc-13593159:

Genes that both shifted in disease and touched estrogen signaling were filtered by two machine learning methods, then checked in a fresh cohort and in single cell liver data.

Chao and the team propose the pair as tissue markers needing blood level proof.
pmc-13593559:

Any resistance, the authors insist, should stop the maneuver at once and trigger imaging checks from several angles plus a contrast injection.
